claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are near-equiatomic and initially solid.
Initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles may contain inherent atomic-scale compositional fluctuations.
High-entropy alloys can exhibit chemical clustering over a wide temperature range.
Cu preferentially segregates to the surfaces of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles in the premelting regime.
Cu is a lower-melting constituent relative to the other elements in the stated FeNiCrCoCu system.
Local compositional fluctuations and surface segregation reduce local cohesive energy.
Local compositional fluctuations and surface segregation enhance defect clustering.
Cu-rich regions create localized energy minima that lower the barrier to atomic mobility.
The reduced local mobility barrier causes premelted domains to nucleate at compositionally heterogeneous or segregated sites.
Atomic diffusion and coalescence of liquid-like regions govern progression from premelting to melting.
Atomistic simulations have predicted the proposed diffusion-and-coalescence progression mechanism.
Atomistic simulations can analyze melting and composition-dependent melting temperatures in compositionally complex materials.
More compositionally heterogeneous or surface-segregated FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will begin premelting at a lower temperature than homogeneous particles.
More compositionally heterogeneous or surface-segregated nanoparticles will exhibit a more gradual melting transition.
Uniformly mixed FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will exhibit a sharper and higher-temperature melting onset.
The melting behavior of homogeneous FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will resemble bulk behavior after accounting for nanoscale size effects.
Particle size, atmosphere, and kinetic factors can alter diffusion, segregation, and the resulting melting response.
Controlled pre-annealing can produce otherwise comparable FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle sets with measurably different degrees of compositional heterogeneity.
